identification: Set of five early Victorian / William IV style bar back dining chairs, c1840-1860: broad curved crest rail, plain turned mid rail, curved stiles, ring-turned tapering front legs on peg feet, sabre-ish back legs. Timber is a red-brown open-grained wood consistent with Australian red cedar (cedar is likely but not confirmed from photos; could be mahogany). Worn brown leather (or leathercloth) seats, upholstered over a stuffed drop-in/slip frame, stained and scuffed. Possible harlequin: the two end chairs in photo 1 look slightly wider and the far-left chair's front seat rail appears reeded, while the middle three have plain moulded rails. Estimate on lot page A$200-300.

viewing_check: Confirm red cedar under the seat rails (pale pink-red, soft, open grain, light, cedary smell). Compare all five: crest, mid rail, front rail (reeded vs plain), seat width and leg turnings. Check for loose joints, rail breaks, repaired back legs, and whether the seat frames are original. Lift a seat to see the frame and any chalk or pencil marks.
